meta.title: LiteGen — One API for every AI image & video model
meta.description: LiteGen is an open-source, OpenAI-compatible proxy for AI image and video generation. Route across OpenAI, Stability, Replicate, Google, Fal, Runway, and Luma with automatic fallback, load balancing, caching, and cost tracking.

hero.title: One API for every AI image & video model
hero.subtitle: LiteGen is the universal proxy for AI image and video generation. Like LiteLLM, but for multimedia — route across every major provider with automatic fallback, load balancing, caching, and cost tracking.
hero.codeCaption: OpenAI-compatible — point your existing client at LiteGen.

howItWorks.heading: One prompt. Every image & video model.
howItWorks.subheading: Send a single OpenAI-style request. LiteGen fans it out to whichever model you want — GPT Image, FLUX, Nano Banana, Veo, Ray — falls back when one is down, and streams the finished image or video straight back. Hover a model to light up its route.
howItWorks.figcaption: Diagram: one OpenAI-style prompt enters the LiteGen gateway, which applies routing, fallback, caching, per-model schemas, key management, and webhooks, then dispatches to image models (OpenAI GPT Image 2, Stability SDXL, Replicate FLUX) and video models (Runway Gen-4, Luma Ray 2) and streams the generated media back.

features.heading: Everything you need to ship generation at scale
features.subheading: A single, self-hosted gateway in front of every provider.

unified.title: Unified API
unified.desc: OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints for image & video across every provider.

routing.title: Smart routing
routing.desc: Fallback chains, weighted round-robin, lowest-cost and lowest-latency strategies.

caching.title: Caching
caching.desc: In-memory cache with configurable TTL to skip duplicate generations.

cost.title: Cost tracking
cost.desc: Per-request cost estimation and aggregate spend analytics.

keys.title: API key management
keys.desc: Create and revoke keys, with weighted key pools and per-key quotas.

observability.title: Observability
observability.desc: Request logging, Prometheus metrics, and structured tracing built in.

dashboard.title: Real-time dashboard
dashboard.desc: Monitor providers, requests, and spend from a React dashboard.

selfhosted.title: Self-hosted
selfhosted.desc: A single binary or Docker, backed by SQLite or Postgres.

socialProof.heading: Industry leaders worldwide
socialProof.subheading: Join the teams shipping generative media on LiteGen.

reference.title: Reference
reference.modelsSub: Every model LiteGen integrates and exactly what each one accepts — generated from the capability registry that powers the gateway.
reference.aspectFrames: a frame image ({roles}) sets the shape of the video, so a ratio applies only without one
reference.aspectFramesUnlessReference: a frame image ({roles}) sets the shape of the video, so a ratio applies only without one, unless a reference image goes with it
reference.aspectFramesDefaultRole: an image sent without a role counts as {role}
reference.noPrompt: not accepted — generates from the input image
reference.formatsNote: as the vendor emits them; the API also lists every container litegen converts to
reference.priceDefault: {price} / {unit} for the default request: every parameter at its default.
reference.priceDefaultOneClip: {price} / {unit} for the default request: every parameter at its default, and one clip.
reference.priceDefaultKeyframes: {price} / {unit} for the default request: every parameter at its default, and keyframes at 0 s and 5 s.
reference.priceRulesIntro: Then these rules, in order, for the request at hand. A price or a rate replaces the price so far; ×, + and − adjust it. The total never goes below {zero}.
reference.priceNote: Prices are the vendor's, exactly as litegen quotes and charges them, before an operator's markup (0% unless one is configured). A price rule reads the request: each parameter as sent, else its default; extra.FIELD, a vendor field sent in extra; references, the reference images sent (references.ROLE, one role's); megapixels, the requested size (1 when no size is sent); duration_seconds, the clip's length; and the views, added_views, keyframes and animations counts.
reference.sourceFormats: the vendor takes {formats}; litegen converts any other mesh it reads
reference.forcedPalette: every pixel is one of them
reference.presets: {n, plural, one {# preset} other {# presets}}: name one by its id, or by the canonical preset in brackets
reference.noPromptSourceModel: not accepted — works on its source_model
reference.noPromptSourceVideo: not accepted — works on its source_video
reference.noPromptSegmentation: not accepted — selects regions of the image with its prompts
reference.restSub: The complete HTTP contract, generated from the OpenAPI spec — for calling LiteGen directly without an SDK.

footer.tagline: The universal proxy for AI image & video generation.
